question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Washout and re-challenge hysteresis assay: Pulse cells with a stimulus, withdraw it, and track AP-1 target gene expression over time. Memory would appear as persistent expression after withdrawal and faster or stronger re-induction on re-challenge, which should be lost in AP-1 mutants lacking DNA binding or dimerization.
2. Acute AP-1 degradation during the rest phase: Use an auxin-inducible degron on FOS or JUN to remove AP-1 after priming but before re-challenge. If AP-1 is the memory substrate, degradation should erase the primed state, while degradation before priming should prevent it from forming.
3. Chromatin persistence time course (ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, H3K27ac): Profile AP-1 occupancy and enhancer accessibility and acetylation at primed and naive sites across a stimulus-withdrawal time course. This tests whether chromatin opening outlasts AP-1 binding and whether it is maintained by AP-1 itself or by a separate epigenetic mechanism.
4. Live single-cell reporter with lineage tracking: Express a fluorescent AP-1 target reporter, prime cells, and follow individual lineages through several divisions by time-lapse imaging. Quantify how long the primed state persists and whether it is inherited by daughter cells, and test whether mitotic bookmarking or chromatin-remodeling perturbations shorten that inheritance.
5. Feedback-loop perturbation and bistability testing: Disrupt candidate positive feedback loops (FOS autoregulation, ATF3 or JUN loops) and co-activator inhibition (p300/CBP or BRD4) in single-cell reporter lines. Memory should scale with loop strength and show bimodal, cell-autonomous persistence rather than a population-average decay, and this should be validated in vivo with a repeated-stimulus model.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Ectopic landing-pad test of locus-autonomous memory
ideas.description: Integrate a primed AP-1 enhancer and a naive copy into the same site-specific landing pad at a neutral genomic locus, then compare retention of the primed state. If memory follows the transplanted enhancer sequence regardless of its native chromatin context, the substrate is local DNA/chromatin; if it depends on the native locus, it is a genome-wide or trans-acting state.

ideas.title: Single-molecule residence-time tracking of JUN and FOS
ideas.description: Tag endogenous JUN and FOS with HaloTag and use single-molecule tracking in naive versus primed cells to measure chromatin-bound dwell times and bound fraction. This tests whether memory is encoded as a change in factor residence kinetics rather than in occupancy, which bulk ChIP cannot distinguish.

ideas.title: Phosphosite knock-in pulse-chase to test post-translational memory
ideas.description: Knock in non-phosphorylatable or phosphomimetic alleles at JUN and FOS regulatory sites (for example JUN Ser63/Ser73) and track phosphoprotein half-lives by pulse-chase phosphoproteomics after priming. Persistent phosphorylation or altered protein turnover after mRNA returns to baseline would show that memory lives in the protein modification state rather than in transcription.

ideas.title: SLAM-seq decomposition of AP-1 target mRNA synthesis versus decay
ideas.description: Use metabolic RNA labeling (SLAM-seq or 4sU) to separately estimate synthesis and degradation rates of AP-1 targets during and after priming. A post-stimulus increase in mRNA half-life, especially if it depends on 3′UTR AU-rich elements, would indicate that memory is encoded as altered mRNA stability rather than as a persistent transcriptional program.

ideas.title: Metabolic gating of memory via acetyl-CoA supply
ideas.description: During the rest phase, vary acetyl-CoA availability with ACLY inhibition, acetate supplementation, or glucose withdrawal, and trace 13C-glucose or 13C-acetate into histone acetylation at primed enhancers. If re-induction tracks acetyl-CoA-dependent acetylation rather than AP-1 levels, memory is metabolically gated and AP-1 may be a reader rather than a writer of the primed state.
